fdd:description.p: FLAC (Free Lossless Audio Codec), Version 1.1.2 is a legacy version of the format which is now standardized through IETF RFC 9639. See FLAC Family for overall description and history of the FLAC format.

Specific to the version 1.1.2, released on Feb 5, 2005, are small decoding speedups for all platforms, small encoding speedups in fast (non-LPC) mode, streaming support in the XMMS plugin, and several bug fixes. For developers there are also a few additions and changes to the metadata API to make working with tags easier. See the changelog entry on xiph.org for complete details. The release notes states: "This release actually wasn't supposed to happen so soon, but needed to be made to fix library naming and build problems in FLAC 1.1.1 that caused trouble for package maintainers, so unless you are having trouble with one of the particular bugs that got fixed in 1.1.2 then there is not much of a need to upgrade." The post Porting from FLAC 1.1.2 to 1.1.3 also describes some specifics differences in the library interfaces from version to version. Comments welcome.

fdd:identificationAndDescription.fdd:shortDescription: Open source bitstream encoding format designed for lossless compression of LPCM audio data, with many of its default parameters tuned to CD-quality music data.
fdd:identificationAndDescription.fdd:productionPhase: Generally used for final-state, end-user delivery.

fdd:localUse.fdd:experience: The Library of Congress has a small number of FLAC files as of June 2026 but it's not possible to determine their version.
fdd:localUse.fdd:preference: See the Library of Congress Recommended Formats Statement for format preferences for audio works.

fdd:sustainabilityFactors.fdd:disclosure: Fully documented. Developed as an open source project; See also FLAC_Family for information about the standardization process through IETF RFC 9639 for later versions.
fdd:sustainabilityFactors.fdd:documentation: Specific information about version 1.1.2, in the form of a Change Log, is available at https://xiph.org/flac/changelog.html. See also FLAC_Family.

fdd:selfDocumentation.p: FLAC's metadata support allows for comprehensive tagging of album info, lyrics, and track titles that may be accessible to screen readers. In common practice, typically audio content is supported by external caption and subtitle formats such as WebVTT. See W3C's Making Audio and Video Media Accessible for more general information about accessible sound and moving image media.
